premise: Working as a bus conductor in Bangalore before rising to become one of Indian cinema's biggest superstars.
hook: He handed out tickets on Bangalore city buses while dreaming of the stage.
key_facts: Worked various jobs including carpentry and as a Bangalore Transport Service bus conductor.
Acted in amateur plays, notably mythological roles in Kannada productions.
Joined the Film and Television Institute of Madras in 1973 to study acting.
Made his cinematic debut in K. Balachander's Tamil film Apoorva Raangangal in 1975.

premise: Accepting the perilous Vostok 1 assignment, knowing the mission's safety systems had barely been tested.
hook: He climbed into a cramped metal sphere atop a ballistic missile, becoming the first human launched into the unknown.
key_facts: Selected from a group of 20 Soviet Air Force fighter pilots for the Vostok program.
Flew aboard Vostok 1 on April 12, 1961, completing one orbit of Earth.
Ejected from the spacecraft at 20,000 feet as per the standard landing design of the time.
Became an international celebrity and hero following the successful historic flight.

premise: Overcoming orphanhood and severe scalp ailments to build a cosmetics empire and become America's first self-made female millionaire.
hook: Suffering from hair loss due to poor sanitation and lack of indoor plumbing, she formulated her own healing tonic.
key_facts: Born on a cotton plantation in Delta, Louisiana, orphaned at age seven.
Worked for decades as a washerwoman before developing hair care products for Black women.
Founded Madam C.J. Walker Manufacturing Company in 1906.
Employed thousands of women as sales agents and became a prominent philanthropist.

premise: Choosing to disobey protocol and report a nuclear warning signal as a false alarm during the height of the Cold War.
hook: Computer screens flashed with incoming US ballistic missiles, and he had minutes to decide whether to launch a retaliatory strike.
key_facts: Served as a lieutenant colonel in the Soviet Air Defense Forces in 1983.
The Oko nuclear early warning system falsely reported five American missiles launched from Montana.
Suspected a computer malfunction because the incoming count was too low for a first strike.
Reported the alert as a false alarm, averting a potential nuclear exchange.

premise: Deciding to fly a single-engine monoplane across the treacherous Atlantic Ocean without a parachute or radio.
hook: He stripped his custom aircraft of every ounce of excess weight—including the radio—to bet his life on a nonstop flight to Paris.
key_facts: Flew the custom-built Spirit of St. Louis from Roosevelt Field, New York, to Paris in May 1927.
Completed the first solo nonstop transatlantic flight in 33.5 hours.
Flew without a forward-facing windshield, relying on a periscope to see ahead.
Became an instant global aviation icon upon landing at Le Bourget Airport.

premise: Keeping all 27 crew members alive for nearly two years after their ship, the Endurance, was crushed by Antarctic pack ice.
hook: After their ship sank beneath the frozen sea, they lived on floating ice floes for months with no radio, no rescue ship, and dwindling food.
key_facts: The Endurance was trapped and crushed by Antarctic ice in 1915.
The crew camped on drifting ice packs for five months before sailing lifeboats to Elephant Island.
Shackleton and five men sailed an 22-foot lifeboat 800 miles across the stormy Southern Ocean to South Georgia Island for help.
Every single member of the stranded expedition survived.

premise: Co-founding Infosys with just $250 borrowed from his wife, growing it into a global IT giant.
hook: He started a multinational tech powerhouse from a spare bedroom with a minuscule loan and a borrowed dining table.
key_facts: Started Infosys in Pune, India, in 1981 with six other software engineers.
Relied on initial seed capital provided by his wife, Sudha Murthy, from her personal savings.
Pioneered the global delivery model for software services out of India.

premise: Deciding to walk through a cleared Angolan minefield in 1997 to force global attention onto the hidden horrors of landmines.
hook: She ignored intense political criticism and walked directly into an active danger zone to force world leaders to ban a deadly weapon.
key_facts: Visited Huambo, Angola, in January 1997 with the Halo Trust to highlight civilian landmine casualties.
Her televised walk was heavily criticized by political opponents as a controversial distraction.
Her campaign directly contributed to the signing of the Ottawa Treaty banning anti-personnel landmines later that year.

premise: Overcoming early orphanhood, poverty, and severe hair loss to build a massive hair care empire and become one of America's first self-made female millionaires.
hook: After losing her own hair to a scalp ailment, she formulated a homemade remedy on her kitchen floor and sold it door-to-door.
key_facts: Born Sarah Breedlove on a cotton plantation in Louisiana, orphaned at age seven.
Worked as a laundress for decades earning meager wages before launching her hair care line in 1905.
Employed thousands of African American women as sales agents across the United States.

premise: Deciding to self-finance the final weeks of production for Pather Panchali by pawning his wife's jewelry and his personal book collection.
hook: When institutional funding dried up completely, he risked everything he owned to finish his debut masterpiece.
key_facts: Shot his debut film Pather Panchali (1955) intermittently over nearly three years using amateur actors and crew.
Pawned valuable family assets, including his wife's jewelry and rare art books, to pay for remaining film stock.
The film went on to win the Best Human Document award at the 1956 Cannes Film Festival.

premise: Inventing a revolutionary tactile reading system as a blind teenager against the resistance of sighted educators.
hook: Blinded in a childhood accident, he took a military night-writing code and simplified it into six raised dots that schools initially banned.
key_facts: Blinded in his father's harness-making workshop at age three after an accidental puncture wound.
Enrolled at the Royal Institution for Blind Youth in Paris, where books were printed in expensive, hard-to-read embossed raised letters.
Invented the six-dot Braille code at age 15, though it was only officially adopted in schools long after his death.
